items.title: Panthers become first NHL team to record natural hat trick in three straight games
items.summary: The Panthers also became the first team in more than 100 years to have at least four hat tricks in the first 10 games of a season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida Panthers forward Carter Verhaeghe recorded a natural hat trick during the team’s 8-3 win over the Seattle Kraken Saturday night. Verhaeghe’s trio of goals made the Panthers the first team in NHL history with natural hat tricks in three consecutive games, after Brady Tkachuk recorded a natural hat trick in Florida’s previous two games. Verhaeghe scored twice late in the first period, then again midway through the second. Panthers forward Sam Bennett also recorded a hat trick in Saturday’s game. Now with four on the season, Florida became the first team in more than 100 years to record four or more hat tricks before its 10th game of the season (the Toronto St. Patricks, later named the Toronto Maple Leafs, had five in 1922-23). The Panthers recorded its first of three natural hat tricks when forward Brady Tkachuk scored three straight in the second period of the team’s 7-3 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets last Tuesday. His brother, Matthew Tkachuk, assisted on all three goals. On Thursday, Brady Tkachuk became the first NHLer to record back-to-back natural hat tricks in Florida’s 3-2 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks . The Panthers are now 5-2-2 through nine games in 2026-27. Matthew Tkatchuk leads the team with 11 assists and 14 points, while Brady Tkachuk and Verhaeghe are tied for a team-leading six goals. Defenseman Seth Jones has one goal and nine assists for 10 points.

items.title: Jets discuss Hellebuyck’s potential return
items.body: Scott Arniel took the podium Saturday afternoon to break down a hockey match, only to provide his two cents on a growing and unpredictable game of chicken involving his NHL club. The Winnipeg Jets head coach spoke less than three minutes following a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes at Canada Life Centre — a game entirely overshadowed by the latest chapter in franchise goaltender Connor Hellebuyck's ongoing trade holdout. “I really don’t care right now on that scenario," started a visibly frustrated Arniel. "My focus is we’ve got St. Louis coming up. I’ve got to do some review against Carolina, there are some areas I want to fix." Just minutes before puck drop, it was reported that Hellebuyck notified the Jets on Oct. 2 — before Winnipeg's first regular-season game — that he planned to end his absence. Rather than welcoming the star netminder back into the fold immediately, the Jets opted to leverage the NHL's collective bargaining agreement. According to reports, the club used Article 15.13, subsection (c)(v) to suspend Hellebuyck for three weeks for failure to report to training camp. The suspension is set to expire on Friday, Oct. 23, just two days before Winnipeg hosts the Montreal Canadiens in the annual Heritage Classic outdoor game at Princess Auto Stadium. "That part, that falls down on Chevy," noted Arniel, noting whatever happens next will be handled by general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff. "I know there is stuff that happens. I’m going to face that one when it happens." "I don’t know what next week is going to look like and at the end of the day, for me, I’ve got 23 guys and all they care about is winning hockey games," added Arniel. items.title: Flyers top Senators to secure first win of season, snap nine-game skid
items.body: With a 3-1 decision on Saturday night against the Ottawa Senators , the Flyers earned their first victory of the season. The win also served to snap the nine-game winless skid to start the season, which was a franchise record. It looked to be the same story for the Flyers as Senators forward Drake Batherson opened the scoring in the second period. But Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone made quick work to negate the deficit, combining for two goals to close out the middle frame. Trevor Zegras added an insurance empty-netter in the third period as the Flyers wrapped up the win. It's a welcome bit of good news for the Flyers, who dug themselves a deep hole early after ending last season with a run to the Eastern Conference semifinals. The Flyers sit in the basement of the East standings and while the season is still young, they'll have to string together more wins like Saturday to claw their way back to relevance.

items.title: Maple Leafs would deal prime asset for difference-maker on blue line
items.body: With Chris Tanev sidelined for multiple weeks with an upper-body injury, the Toronto Maple Leafs could look to make a splash in order to boost their defensive corps. Although Tanev skated on Saturday, the Maple Leafs have made it clear that they aren't interested in a "Band-Aid solution" to fill the open spot, according to Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman. "(The Maple Leafs) have said that they will pay a premium asset if they believe that they are getting a difference-maker on the blue line," Friedman reported on the latest segment of Saturday Headlines . "They've told people they're not moving what they consider 'A-assets' for a B-level replacement." Toronto head coach Jim Hillier said Thursday that he is comfortable with the defenceman currently on the Maple Leafs' roster, but added that it would take a team effort to replace Tanev's impact. The 36-year-old defenceman was hurt in Toronto's 6-3 road win over the Colorado Avalanche last Saturday and placed on injured reserve Monday. Tanev skated in five shifts in the first period before leaving the game. The oft-injured Tanev was limited to 11 games last season due to spine and groin injuries as well as a concussion. He has one assist in six games this season. In its first two games without Tanev, Toronto surrendered 10 total goals across a pair of 5-4 losses to the Utah Mammoth and Buffalo Sabres. Adding a defenceman who can step in and contribute right away isn't the only type of move being considered for the Maple Leafs' roster. "They've also indicated that they would consider getting a younger player (by) moving an older guy," Friedman said Saturday. "So, that's what Toronto is looking at right now." The Maple Leafs currently have the fourth oldest roster in the NHL by average age.

Five minutes and 12 seconds into the first period, Lakovic found the back of the net for the first time as a professional, beating Providence Bruins goaltender Simon Zajíček . The Bears’ rookie winger was the beneficiary of a good bounce. After Louie Belpedio’s shot from the top of the left circle was blocked, Spencer Smallman picked up the loose puck in the bumper position and sent a quick pass to the Washington Capitals ‘ 2025 first-round pick in the right circle. Lakovic’s quick one timer beat Zajíček as he extended out to cover the net. The goal was one of several big moments Lakovic had during the game where he put up a team-high and AHL career-high six shots. Lakovic nearly scored again in the second period after he found a loose puck near the crease and fired it on net toward Zajíček. The biscuit squeaked through the Bruins netminder’s body, but after a goal review, AHL officials deemed that the puck was swept back by a Bruins defender’s stick before it fully crossed the goal line. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Dallas’ Roope Hintz did not have possession and control of the puck when he preceded it into the offensive zone and was therefore in an off-side position prior to Jason Robertson ’s goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 8:02 (11:58 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google The Washington Capitals have a new player of the game award, and it’s a vintage piece of equipment with special significance. Future Washington Capitals captain Tom Wilson revealed the special item after the Capitals defeated the New Jersey Devils 4-2 in a Saturday matinee at Capital One Arena. “I think we’re going with ‘Legend of the Game,'” Wilson said, sliding out an Alex Ovechkin rookie-era helmet from his Bauer bag. “We can only start with one guy. Our leader.” Wilson then handed Ovechkin his old bucket, which he briefly affixed on his head. “I’m still young, by the way,” Ovechkin said. “All right, guys. I think today, great job [like] Carbs said, ’40 hard minutes.’ LT, great job, but Vincent.” (Ovechkin pronounced Vincent in a heavy French accent.) Desharnais then threw on the helmet before dropping some of Ovechkin’s rookie vernacular. “Sick,” he said as the team laughed. “Stay f***ing hot, boys. Let’s f***ing keep going.” Monumental Sports Network host Tarik El-Bashir reported that the idea was Wilson’s alone. Ovechkin first wore the mirrored tinted visor, which gave the young Russian superstar a distinctive, RoboCop-like appearance, 21 years ago during his debut season in the NHL, and it caused controversy. Devils goaltender Martin Brodeur complained that it gave Ovechkin an unfair advantage because opponents couldn’t see his eyes. NHL general managers later voted 29–1 against allowing mirrored visors in 2006, with Washington’s George McPhee as the lone dissenter, though the prohibition was never formally written into the rulebook. Ovechkin reluctantly switched to a smoky-tinted visor, but nearly two decades later, he still considers the original his favorite.

Through training and rehab, Clark's journey back to playing hockey is an emotional story of perseverance. All Kyle Clark wanted was to go outside and have fun with his buddies. It was one of the last things he told his parents before his life flipped upside down. He was heading into his U-18 season, pursuing junior opportunities and attending prospect camps. Just a week before the accident, he played in a junior showcase that gave him more exposure. items.body: Register Login Canadiens Activate Oliver Kapanen, Place Florian Xhekaj On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 17, 2026 1:00 pm The Canadiens have made a pair of roster moves in advance of their game tonight against Buffalo. The team announced that center Oliver Kapanen will make his season debut, meaning he has been activated off injured reserve. To make room for him on the roster, winger Florian Xhekaj has been placed on IR. The 23-year-old played in three preseason games last month and appeared to have sustained a lower-body injury in the final one. He was given a day-to-day designation at the time but wound up missing more than three weeks because of the issue in the end. Kapanen was one of Montreal’s more pleasant surprises last season. While he faded down the stretch, he still finished 11th in Calder Trophy voting and made a handful of appearances in the playoffs. He’s expected to take Owen Beck ’s spot on the fourth line to start. items.body: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Matt Marton-Imagn Images Have NHL Fans Finally Reached A Breaking Point? Especially in U.S. markets, October has always been the worst month for NHL attendance. But even with that in mind, there are teams that are turning in some surprising numbers early in the season. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs got a tough update on one of their key players, as they announced on Saturday that center John Tavares is week-to-week with a lower-body injury. Tavares sustained the injury during Thursday’s 5-4 overtime loss to the Buffalo Sabres . Nick Paul and Josh Norris were tangled with each other in the middle of the ice, and when Paul shoved Norris onto the ice, Norris fell into a passing Tavares, taking the 36 year old’s legs out from underneath him and causing him to fall awkwardly on the ice. He remained on the ice for a bit before requiring assistance to the dressing room, and did not return to the game. According to reports from the Leafs’ media, the team also mentioned that Tavares’ week-to-week designation could keep him out of the lineup for anywhere between one to six weeks, which would potentially keep him out of the lineup until the end of November. Based on the provided timeline, Tavares is projected to miss anywhere between four and 19 games. At this point in time, the Leafs have not announced if Tavares has been placed on injured reserve or long-term injured reserve, nor have they announced any corresponding roster moves. One will likely be needed though, as the Leafs are down to only 12 forwards on their roster. The injury is a tough break for Tavares, who was continuing on his strong production even into late 30s with two goals and five assists for seven points in seven games before the injury. It also comes only two games after Tavares had missed a game to attend the birth of his child. With Tavares out, Easton Cowan moves up to the second line to play alongside Nick Paul and Kirill Marchenko, a combination which has only played 13 seconds together in passing this season.

It’s just unbelievable. To wear that NHL crest for the first time, to take that lap, it was a night that I’ll remember all my life.” For Hautamäki, Tuesday in Detroit was a night nearly 15 years in the making since he stopped playing junior hockey as a 16-year-old and picked up a whistle. IIHF director of officiating Scott Zelkin identified Hautamäki during a seven-year run rising through the ranks of Liiga, Finland’s top pro league, and he then burst onto the NHL’s radar at international events like the world juniors and world championship. items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby passes Thornton for seventh in NHL all-time assists
items.summary: Sidney Crosby’s legend continues to grow, as he climbed up the NHL’s all-time assists list.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Sidney Crosby’s start to the 2026-27 season might not be as productive as hoped, but his legend continued to grow on Friday night, as he rose up the NHL’s all-time assist list. The Pittsburgh Penguins captain posted the 1,110th assist of his illustrious career against the Colorado Avalanche in a 5-2 loss. While the result didn’t fall Pittsburgh’s way, the point pushed Crosby past Joe Thornton on the league’s all-time assists list, into seventh place. Crosby now sits 25 assists behind Paul Coffey, whose 1,135 assists are good for sixth place, but well behind Wayne Gretzky’s lead of 1,963 assists, which remains more career assists than any other NHL player has points. In terms of points, Crosby is also approaching the top five, with his 1,766 only 32 short of fifth-place in all-time points, Ron Francis. At 39, Crosby’s impact has slightly diminished with the Penguins. Playing alongside Kris Letang and Evgeni Malkin in his 22nd season with the club, the trio has become the longest-serving trio in NHL history. However, Crosby has two goals and three assists for five points in eight games, while the Penguins have managed only three wins in those contests. Despite being in the twilight of his career, Crosby will look to return to at least a point-per-game pace in the near future. Last season, he netted 29 goals and 45 assists for 74 points in 68 games, missing time due to an injury sustained during Canada’s silver-medal run at the Milan Cortina 2026 Olympics. Through his entire 22-year career, he has never finished a season below a point-per-game total. After falling to the Avalanche on Friday, Crosby and the Penguins will turn their attention towards a Saturday night clash with the Vegas Golden Knights as the back end of back-to-back road games. items.body: DENVER — Nathan MacKinnon had three assists and a power-play goal, Artturi Lehkonen scored twice and the Colorado Avalanche rallied to beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-2 on Friday night. T.J. Hughes scored his first NHL goal, while Mackenzie Blackwood settled in after a shaky start to stop 29 shots. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust gave Pittsburgh a 2-0 lead after scoring 29 seconds apart midway through the first period. The Avalanche erupted for five straight tallies, including three in the second period. Colorado finished one of four on the power play in the Avalanche debut of assistant coach Brett McLean. He's in charge of the unit after Dave Hakstol left to take over as head coach of the men's hockey program at Arizona State. Lehkonen's second goal tied it 25 seconds into the second period. Captain Gabriel Landeskog had a goal nearly four minutes later for his 83rd career go-ahead score. He's tied with Mikko Rantanen for sixth-most in Avalanche history. Hall of Famer Joe Sakic tops the list with 210. Hughes got free down low and poked in a pass from MacKinnon. He was hugged by Cale Makar and then playfully squirted with water by Landeskog as Hughes made his way past the bench. Sidney Crosby notched his 1,110th career assist to move into sole possession of seventh place in NHL history. He's also one assist shy of matching Ray Bourque (1,111 with Boston) for the most in league history with a one franchise. MacKinnon improved to 12-6-3 when playing against Crosby, his good buddy from Nova Scotia. MacKinnon was awarded a penalty shot, but was stopped by Arturs Silovs. Avalanche: Two-game road swing starting Monday night at Philadelphia.

items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have placed winger Miles Wood on injured reserve.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Place Miles Wood On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 16, 2026 8:00 pm The injury list has been pretty long already this season for the Maple Leafs, who find themselves down several regulars in the early going. Now, one of the players called up to cover for those injuries is injured himself without even playing one game. Per the NHL’s media site, winger Miles Wood has been placed on injured reserve. The 31-year-old cleared waivers back in training camp and was assigned to the minors but found himself on the move soon after as he was moved to Toronto as part of the Kirill Marchenko trade. His inclusion appeared to be more for salary cap purposes as he carries a $2.5MM cap charge for the next three years, a hefty price tag for someone to play in the AHL. He earned that money over a decade’s worth of games, where he has 99 goals and 97 assists in 567 appearances. Wood remained on assignment to the Marlies early in the season and hadn’t seen game action prior to his recall last week. He got into some practices and evidently sustained some sort of injury, although the nature is undisclosed and there’s no word on a timeline for his return. Toronto has a little under $5MM remaining in LTIR room, per PuckPedia . That pool will be reduced by $3.25MM in the coming days with Dakota Joshua ’s pending return but even so, they can easily afford to carry Wood on IR for the time being. If Wood is eventually deemed to miss at least 10 games and 24 days, he’ll be eligible to be transferred to LTIR himself. The Maple Leafs now have one open spot on their active roster, though that could be given to Joshua over the next few days.

items.body: Allowing third-most goals-against in NHL entering game against Rangers Saturday Rick Bowness said everyone associated with the Columbus Blue Jackets "should be very angry with where we are." The coach, speaking on Friday, said he especially was bothered by the fact that the Blue Jackets have allowed an average of 4.20 goals per game, tied for the third most in the NHL. "We're 30th in the League in goals-against -- 30th," Bowness said. "I've never coached a team that was 30th in the League in goals-against." The Blue Jackets (2-3-0), who host the New York Rangers at Nationwide Arena on Saturday (7 p.m. ET; CBJHN, CBJNHL, MSG), haven't played since Tuesday, a 7-3 home loss to the Florida Panthers. That followed a 5-3 loss at the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. They have allowed at least three goals in four of their five games and are 1-3-0 after a 6-3 win against the Buffalo Sabres in their season opener Oct. 1. After the loss to the Panthers, Bowness voiced his frustration with his team. "We beat ourselves in St. Louis. We beat ourselves tonight," Bowness said. "So you have to hope, you've got to believe, that that performance tonight will embarrass them enough to stop this, right? Because if they're not embarrassed by that, we don't want them on the team. It's as simple as that. "I'm not a babysitter. I'm too old to be a babysitter for these guys. You're a professional athlete, prepare yourself to play properly." This is not the first time that Bowness has called out his team. Last season, after the Blue Jackets had been eliminated from Stanley Cup Playoff contention, Bowness said if he returned to Columbus this season, he would be "changing the culture." items.title: Why are teams struggling to sell out games?
items.summary: The Vegas Golden Knights snapped a nine-year sellout streak this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images The NHL is a gate-driven league. You may have heard this said a time or two before. While leagues like the NFL and NBA generate a major portion of their revenue from broadcasting deals, the NHL still relies much more heavily on in-person attendance. It can’t be a great sign, then, that teams around the league have been failing to sell out early in the season. The Vegas Golden Knights snapped their nine-year sellout streak on October 8, when they hit just 92% attendance for a game against the Toronto Maple Leafs . items.title: Ducks’ rebuild provides blueprint for Flames to follow
items.summary: As the Flames embark on their own rebuild, the Ducks are beginning to look an awful lot like the blueprint GM Craig Conroy would love to follow, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: That was the timeline Pat Verbeek had in mind shortly after he took the wheel in Anaheim, a franchise that needed to tear things down before it could dream of building something special again. The goal wasn't to win a Stanley Cup in five years. It wasn't even to guarantee a playoff spot. It was to become a team that could start contending for a sprinkling of spring hockey. As the Calgary Flames embark on their own uncomfortable transition, Verbeek's Anaheim Ducks are beginning to look an awful lot like the blueprint Craig Conroy would love to follow. The similarities aren't lost on Verbeek, who has watched his young Ducks take a significant step forward after years of accumulating draft picks, developing talent and carefully adding veterans to help the kids grow. "When I talk to Connie, yeah," Verbeek said of the parallels between Anaheim's rebuild and Calgary's. "Transitioning is probably the hardest thing to do, not wanting to take a step back, but just kind of gaining a little ground every year.” In a one-on-one chat outside the Ducks dressing room, Verbeek said that when he arrived in Anaheim in Feb. 2022, his first instinct was to try to retain the veteran foundation on a team that missed the playoffs three years running. But Josh Manson, Hampus Lindholm and Rickard Rakell couldn't be signed to new deals, forcing the general manager to change course. That pivot, as he calls it, became the foundation of the rebuild. Rather than cling to a group that wasn't going to take the Ducks where they wanted to go, Verbeek traded those veterans and began stockpiling draft picks, putting an emphasis on identifying and developing young talent. According to a team announcement , the Kraken recalled defenseman Ty Nelson from the AHL’s Coachella Valley Firebirds. Seattle had an open roster spot before the transaction, so no corresponding roster move was necessary. Seattle selected Nelson, 22, with the 68th overall pick (third-round) in the 2022 NHL Draft. The Toronto, ON, native played for the OHL’s North Bay Battalion at the time, scoring 40 goals and 128 points in 121 games in his two post-draft campaigns. Nelson has continued his strong two-way play in the AHL. Since debuting with AHL Coachella Valley in 2024-25, he has registered 17 goals and 71 points in 140 games with a +34 rating. He has puck-moving skills similar to those of other smaller defensemen. Still, despite standing at 5’10″and weighing 198 lbs, Nelson plays extremely large. They aren’t all bone-crushing hits, but he plays with an extremely high motor and sacrifices his body almost every shift. Unfortunately, despite his strong play with the Firebirds, Nelson hasn’t made his NHL debut. Depending on the severity of Montour’s injury, that could change during his current recall. Even without Montour, Seattle maintains a solid mix of handedness in their defensive corps. They could consider removing Cale Fleury for a game or two to provide Nelson with an opportunity.

items.title: ‘Should all be very angry’: Cooler heads not prevailing for Blue Jackets’ Bowness
items.body: The Columbus Blue Jackets coach continued his public tirade over his team's defence on Friday three days after it suffered a 7-3 loss to the Floridaa Panthers. "Right now, we should all be very angry at where we are," Bowness told reporters . "You look at our team. We’re 30th in the league in goals against. I’ve never coached a team that was 30th in the league in goals against … I’m mad. I keep seeing 30th goals against. That bothers me." Columbus, which sits 3-2 on the season, is tied with the Los Angeles Kings for third-last in the NHL at 4.20 goals against per game. The Blue Jackets fell apart in the second period of the Panthers loss, allowing four goals including a natural hat trick from Brady Tkachuk. Forward Mathieu Olivier did his team no favours either, taking an ill-advised five-minute major penalty for slashing, which led to his subsequent ejection and another goal against. "Yeah. They’re like I am. They’re not happy where they are," he said. The 71-year-old coach ripped into his players in the immediate aftermath of the game on Tuesday, calling the performance "embarrassing." "You gotta believe that performance will embarrass them enough to stop this, right?" Bowness told reporters . "Because if they're not embarrassed by that, we don't want them on the team. Simple as that." "I know it looks bad, but I believe in what we're doing. I believe in them. I believe we can fix the problems," the bench boss added. "That all being said, if (the game) doesn't get their attention, then they're on the wrong team." Blue Jackets players will have their first chance to do just that when they return to the ice Saturday for a home date against the New York Rangers.

items.body: In the midst of a close divisional game against the Buffalo Sabres, Gavin McKenna found himself stapled to the bench from halfway through the second period through to the final buzzer. He played just 6:36 in total. To my memory, it was one of the longest benchings of a non-fourth line player in years in Toronto, and given it happened to their recent number one overall draft pick, we’re going to talk about it. We’re going to talk about it partially because it’s McKenna, who at times has been electric in his first eight NHL games. But we're also going to talk about it because it felt like a microcosm of a strategic coaching problem in the loss. They stapled talent to the bench while increasing the minutes for their defensive veterans, trying to hold on to a two-goal lead rather than continuing to take it to a Sabres team whose blue line – without Rasmus Dahlin – was badly struggling to manage the Leafs' talent up-front. So, the kid played under seven minutes, and didn't see the ice at all in the game’s second half. Why? items.body: Register Login Midday Notes: Raddysh, Back, Xhekaj By Marcus Antonelli | at October 16, 2026 11:26 am The New York Rangers have recalled Taylor Raddysh from Hartford, their AHL affiliate, and have sent down Jaroslav Chmelar . Raddysh joins the team having played the start of his 2026-27 campaign with three goals for five points in five AHL contests. The former second-round pick is in the second year of a two-year, $1.5MM AAV contract. At age 28, Raddysh has solidified his professional profile as a depth piece for an organization that can provide some worthy second-hand offense. In his first year with New York, he scored 19 points in 68 games. Historically, Raddysh has seen a near 40-point campaign with the Blackhawks back in 2022-23. Even then, penalty killing and defensive prowess are valuable things the Rangers will need out of him, which he has been prominent in. Chmelar, in comparison, has been averaging less NHL time than what Raddysh usually provides in a similar role. The former fifth-round pick out of Czechia has started his first seven NHL games in 2026-27 with around eight minutes of ice time at 5-on-5 and has yet to produce a point. The 23-year-old has fared better in the AHL, having scored 56 points across three seasons, totaling 124 games. He could benefit from more minutes, similar to how Cole Beaudoin wouldn’t receive quality NHL ice time yet. He’s known as a forward who attacks straight with his speed, but has areas to improve in his handling, which, if mastered, could help with more offensive opportunities.

items.body: Actor, survivor joins cause that has become ‘personal’ for team DETROIT -- Dave Coulier stood outside the Detroit Red Wings dressing room Thursday, hanging out with fellow “Full House” star Andrea Barber. The 67-year-old actor had come to Little Caesars Arena for two reasons: One, he grew up a huge Red Wings fan in St. Clair Shores, Michigan. Two, Detroit was hosting Hockey Fights Cancer Night. Coulier is a cancer survivor. He and Barber wore special Red Wings Hockey Fights Cancer jerseys to a game against the Philadelphia Flyers, raising awareness and money for the cause. “Early screenings saved my life twice now with Non-Hodgkin lymphoma and carcinoma,” Coulier said. “It makes a big difference. It’s not sexy, but get that prostate exam, get that colonoscopy, get those mammograms. I’m encouraging people to do so.” Hockey Fights Cancer, a joint initiative of the NHL and NHL Players’ Association, is in its 28th season and has generated more than $53 million in total fundraising. Since partnering with the V Foundation in 2023, it has raised more than $12.3 million for cancer research and awarded 42 research grants. This night was particularly meaningful for the Red Wings. Jenny Baumann, the wife of physical therapist and assistant athletic trainer Russ Baumann, passed away due to cancer Saturday. She was 55. Red Wings coach Todd McLellan choked up as he talked about it. This past weekend we lost Jenny Baumann. Jenny is the wife of Physical Therapist and Assistant Athletic Trainer, Russ Baumann. items.body: We’re still less than three weeks into the 2026-27 campaign and it’s easy to jump to conclusions about things that may turn out to be silly a month from now. Still, it’s fun to look around the league at some anomalies and ponder if they could become trends. Maybe a team that was destined to be a basement dweller catches fire in the first half-dozen games and is sitting near the top of its division. Or there might be a player that never really had a nose for the net who is suddenly shooting the lights out. What about the goalie that struggled mightily last year who is all of a sudden unbeatable? History tells many of these things won’t hold up for 80-plus games, but it doesn’t make them any less eye-popping for now. There’s also the odd early-season trend that turns out to have legs and be sustainable. The Pittsburgh Penguins from a year ago are a good example: after missing the playoffs for three straight seasons, the Pens won six of their first eight games and no one thought it would last. However, five months later, Pittsburgh claimed a playoff spot and never really slowed down. items.body: LAS VEGAS — Rasmus Andersson knows what Calgary Flames fans are going through right now. He spent nine years with the organization, arriving as a 21-year-old and leaving as a 29-year-old. He built a family in Calgary and experienced the highs and lows of playing in a market where hockey means an awful lot to people. So when he sees his former team struggling through the earliest stages of a rebuild, he understands the frustration. He also knows there's a bigger picture at play. “You never want to see your old team struggle, right?” said the Vegas defender. “But at the same time, they went out and said it's a rebuild, and this is what the fans asked for.” It's a difficult balance for everyone involved. Fans want to see progress, young players need time to develop, and management is trying to build a team capable of competing for years to come. This will take time. Lots of it. Andersson's point isn't that Calgary supporters shouldn't be frustrated. It's that rebuilding is rarely a straight line, and patience becomes particularly important when there are growing pains, like the team’s 1-6 start, arrive. “They can't get impatient,” said Andersson, who has long monitored the pulse of the fans closer than most. “I don't read about it the same way as I did, but it still pops up here and there — I still see some comments like, ‘fire the coach, do this, do this.’ “Did guys think you could win seven in a row to start the season when you guys go out and say you want to rebuild? Through the first half of the game, it was a normal night for the rookie winger, as he had nine shifts and 6:36 of ice time as the midway point of the middle frame approached. But then suddenly, that was his night. With a 2-2 tie at the time, McKenna never touched the ice again, whether that be the rest of the second period, the entirety of the third period, or in overtime. So what was the problem? Was McKenna hurt? Was there something in his game that night that caused Leafs head coach Jim Hiller to bench the rookie in hopes of learning his lesson? “That was my decision,” Hiller told the media after the game. “We went for a stretch, he sat through the penalties. Now that I’ve sat him for so long, I probably should’ve got him out in the third.” The penalties in question are the hooking minor that went to Oliver Ekman-Larsson at the 14:35 mark of the second, the hooking minor that went to Morgan Rielly at the 18:07 mark, and the interference minor that went to Zach Benson at the 18:33 mark. McKenna is not on the Leafs’ penalty kill unit, so he never went out during those stretches, and also has generally not played minutes for the Leafs’ 4v4 and 3v3 units either. After all that was lost in the shuffle, apparently Hiller opted to not play him the rest of the game. items.title: Keller scores twice, Mammoth hand Oilers first regulation loss of season
items.summary: EDMONTON -- Clayton Keller scored twice, and the Utah Mammoth won 4-2 to hand the Edmonton Oilers their first regulation loss of the season Thursday at Rogers Place.
